title: The Thing My God Doth Hate
description: The Thing My God Doth Hate in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 340.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: The thing my God doth hate That I no more may do, Thy crea-ture, Lord, a-gain cre_-ate, And all my soul re-new; My soul shall then, like thine, Ab-hor the thing un-clean, And, sanc-ti-fied by love di-vine, For ev-er cease from sin.

lines: The thing my God doth hate
That I no more may do,
My soul shall then, like thine,
The Spirit's law of life divine,
O write it in my heart!
The law of liberty from sin,
In me, O Lord, fulfil again

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
